jokes.explanation: The saltwater wisdom is the kind of thing that sounds deep but is actually somewhat obvious — which is the joke about Eagleton Ron's philosophy. Competent character work.

jokes.text: Leslie, remove this man before I commit an act of violence against him. / Whatever you do, I won't fight back.
jokes.setup: Eagleton Ron has offered parting wisdom to Pawnee Ron
jokes.punchline: Ron's threat of violence is met by Eagleton Ron's pledge of non-violence — a perfect final joke showing how opposite they are: Ron's response is force, Eagleton Ron's is pacifism
jokes.explanation: Excellent final exchange for the Eagleton Ron arc. The call-and-response of violence threat vs. non-violence pledge crystallizes everything about both characters in two lines. 'Whatever you do, I won't fight back' as a final parting shot is actually a form of moral victory, which would enrage Ron even more. Strong structure and perfect character integration.

jokes.text: After I defeated him in an epic struggle, E.R.I.C. is gone. He's been replaced by T.O.M. — Town-wide Organizational Matrix.
jokes.setup: Tom claimed he was going to talk trash to defeat Eric; E.R.I.C. is now gone
jokes.punchline: Tom's confessional frames deleting a software program as an 'epic struggle' he personally defeated — and has replaced E.R.I.C. with T.O.M., a new acronym that happens to spell his name
jokes.explanation: A perfect payoff to the E.R.I.C. arc. Tom has replaced a computer program named E.R.I.C. with one named T.O.M. — the Town-wide Organizational Matrix that spells his name. This is Tom Haverford's definitive character joke: he turned talking trash about a computer into a win and branded the replacement with his own name. 'After I defeated him in an epic struggle' about deleting software is inspired. One of Tom's best moments.

jokes.text: No, I have a ton of work to do. Plus, my DVR is 13 months pregnant with episodes of Scandal.
jokes.setup: Someone asks Craig about his plans for the night
jokes.punchline: 'My DVR is 13 months pregnant with episodes of Scandal' — an extended metaphor for a packed DVR that is over-specific (13 months, pregnant) and delivered with Craig's characteristic intensity
jokes.explanation: An outstanding line. '13 months pregnant' as a measure of DVR fullness is a wonderfully strange and specific metaphor — beyond full-term, past due, absurdly engorged. The specificity of '13 months' (not 9, not 12) is a perfect Craig touch. This is highly quotable and captures the character's intensity about something completely mundane.

jokes.text: Scandal's my favorite show. I love every character, except for... / Mellie. / Oh! Of course you like Scandal! Because you're amazing! I love you.
jokes.setup: Craig mentions Scandal; Donna finishes his sentence about Mellie
jokes.punchline: Donna's ability to predict exactly which character Craig would hate triggers Craig's complete emotional breakdown — 'I love you' — because being understood is his ultimate need
jokes.explanation: A beautifully structured character moment. Craig's intensity throughout the episode is entirely about caring — and being cared for. When Donna predicts his exact Scandal opinion, Craig's emotional explosion ('I love you') is both funny and surprisingly sweet. The pause before 'Mellie' and Craig's reaction is a perfect comedic beat. Strong character work for both.

jokes.text: And no matter what happens with this job, I will always love you. / Excuse me! Who even are you?
jokes.setup: Craig has just declared his love for Donna
jokes.punchline: Leslie's interruption — 'Excuse me! Who even are you?' — expressing genuine bewilderment at Craig's emotional intensity as a newcomer
jokes.explanation: Good reaction beat. Leslie's 'Who even are you?' directed at Craig's outburst is both Leslie's exasperation and a meta-acknowledgment that Craig is a new character making big declarations. The line works in context and characterizes Leslie's current state.

jokes.text: How's your salad? / Well, it's called the 'Good Earth Salad,' but really, it's just cheese, toffee, and gummy bear worms. / This town is really unhealthy.
jokes.setup: Ben and Chris are having dinner, reminiscing about their auditing days
jokes.punchline: Chris's salad reveals Pawnee's health crisis in miniature — a dish named 'Good Earth Salad' contains no vegetables, only cheese, toffee, and gummy worms
jokes.explanation: A well-constructed joke in the Pawnee-is-unhealthy tradition. 'Good Earth Salad' is a beautiful piece of ironic naming for something containing gummy bear worms and toffee. The list of 'cheese, toffee, and gummy bear worms' is funny in its specificity and progressive wrongness. Good callback to the mega-diabetes joke's theme.

jokes.text: I forgot that this part of being accounting bros was actually pretty depressing. I mean, after the intense, almost meth-like high of solving accounting puzzles, we were always just beat at the end of the day.
jokes.setup: Ben and Chris are reflecting on their old auditing life
jokes.punchline: 'The intense, almost meth-like high of solving accounting puzzles' — Ben describing accounting work as producing a narcotic high comparable to methamphetamine
jokes.explanation: Excellent Ben character joke. The comparison of accounting satisfaction to a meth high is both a character-specific exaggeration (only Ben would experience this) and a genuinely funny image. 'Almost meth-like' with the qualifier 'almost' is a nice touch — he's keeping it honest. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: You'd exercise. I'd re-watch Twin Peaks, then hit the Twin Peaks message boards and read The Secret Diary of Laura Palmer to find Easter Eggs I'd missed.
jokes.setup: Ben and Chris describe what they used to do after long auditing days in empty towns
jokes.punchline: Ben's after-work ritual — rewatching Twin Peaks, message boards, and reading the companion novel to find Easter eggs — is a perfectly specific portrait of a nerdy introvert's comfort routine, contrasted with Chris's simple 'exercise'
jokes.explanation: The specificity is everything. Ben didn't just watch TV — he watched Twin Peaks, then went to the message boards, then read the companion novel for Easter eggs. This is a complete portrait of a certain kind of obsessive nerd, contrasted perfectly with Chris's monosyllabic 'you'd exercise.' Strong Ben character integration.

jokes.text: Something healthy! A cherry tomato. / Nope. / A gumball. / Ooh!
jokes.setup: Chris reaches into what might be a salad or snack, hoping for something healthy
jokes.punchline: He finds a cherry tomato (healthy) but it turns out not to be — then identifies a gumball (not healthy) and his excitement at the gumball underlines Pawnee's inescapable food environment
jokes.explanation: A physical comedy beat that works in context. Chris's reversal — rejecting the tomato, embracing the gumball — is a funny beat that ties together the Pawnee-unhealthy theme. Economy is good; the joke is in the 'Ooh!' at the gumball.

tmdb_overview: Leslie tries to calm a minor scandal that gets blown out of proportion. Tom tries to impress a new love interest, while Ben convinces Ron to prepare a will.
insight: Six doppelgängers identified across 54 jokes—absurdist escalation anchors a high-density character showcase.
